letter.speaker: The letter
letter.text:
Dear Occupant,
We regret to inform you that tomorrow has gone missing.

letter.speaker: The letter
letter.text: As you are the only available person, locating it has become your responsibility. Please refrain from dying during the investigation. The paperwork is tremendous.

letter.speaker: The letter
letter.text:
Report to the house at the end of Forgotten Street. Ask for Fig.
Sincerely, the Department of Unfinished Things.

letter.speaker: Visitor
letter.text:
There wasn't a house at the end of this street yesterday.
Then again, apparently we aren't doing tomorrow either.

fig_street.speaker: Visitor
fig_street.text: I wasn't aware I had an appointment.

fig_street.speaker: Visitor
fig_street.text: Are you a cat wearing a tie?

fig_street.speaker: Fig
fig_street.text: I'm upper management. The tie is mandatory.

fig_street.speaker: Visitor
fig_street.text: I received a letter about tomorrow.

fig_street.speaker: Fig
fig_street.text: Yes, very regrettable. We'd planned to have one.

fig_street.speaker: Fig
fig_street.text: Come inside. The Guestbook will want a word. It likes arguments.

mirror.speaker: Visitor
mirror.text: The Guestbook won't accept my name.

mirror.speaker: Fig
mirror.text: Naturally. This house admits someone who might have arrived. Names are less reliable than you think.

mirror.speaker: Fig
mirror.text: Take this pocket mirror. It's not very good at showing what exists.

mirror.speaker: Fig
mirror.text: To find what nearly did. We call it The Almost. The rooms stay put; their possibilities are less well behaved.

mirror.speaker: Fig
mirror.text: Press Space to look into The Almost. You can return whenever you wish. If you get stuck, ask me—or open your notebook with N.

book_declined.speaker: Guestbook
book_declined.text: DECLINED. YOU ARE NOT WHO YOU THINK YOU ARE.

book_declined.speaker: Fig
book_declined.text: Efficient, though. The book expects a kind of guest, not a name.

book_needs_clue.speaker: Guestbook
book_needs_clue.text: The expected guest has no written name. Find the title the house remembers.

book_needs_clue.speaker: Visitor
book_needs_clue.text: Something in this room must tell me who it expects. Perhaps something that isn't quite here.

portrait_here.speaker: Visitor
portrait_here.text: An unfinished portrait. Its brass nameplate is completely blank.

portrait_here.speaker: Visitor
portrait_here.text: Whoever sat for it seems to have left before they arrived.

portrait_almost.speaker: Visitor
portrait_almost.text: There is someone in the portrait now. Not quite me. Someone who could have been.

portrait_almost.speaker: Visitor
portrait_almost.text: A title, not a name. I'll write it in my notebook.

book_accepted.speaker: Visitor
book_accepted.text: The chandelier just bowed to me.

book_accepted.speaker: Fig
book_accepted.text:
We do try.
You'll do. Probably.

book_accepted.speaker: Visitor
book_accepted.text: Both doors clicked open. And a red notice just appeared on the left sideboard.

notice.speaker: Departmental notice
notice.text:
PROPERTY STATUS: UNFINISHED.
CLOSURE: NEXT TOMORROW.

notice.speaker: Fig
notice.text: It's much more reassuring than 'last yesterday.'

notice.speaker: Visitor
notice.text: Someone has stopped the clocks. Someone else wants to close the house. I think these might be the same problem.

notice.speaker: Fig
notice.text: The kitchen is through the door on the left. Mabel makes tea when she has something not to tell you.

clock.speaker: Visitor
clock.text: Eleven fifty-nine. The pendulum is waiting politely for a future.

clock.speaker: Visitor
clock.text: A tiny label reads: PLEASE DO NOT WIND WITHOUT TOMORROW.

books.speaker: Visitor
books.text:
How to Win Arguments With Dust.
Volume II: When the Dust Has a Point.

books.speaker: Fig
books.text: An excellent volume. The first edition was defeated by a shelf.

tea.speaker: Visitor
tea.text: Two cups. One warm, one full of a remarkably convincing absence.

tea.speaker: Fig
tea.text: We keep a place for someone who nearly stayed.

flowers.speaker: Visitor
flowers.text: The roses smell of rain and a birthday I almost remembered.

flowers.speaker: Visitor
flowers.text: A little card says: Everything unfinished still needs watering. — Mabel

street_sign.speaker: Street sign
street_sign.text:
FORGOTTEN STREET
Please remember to leave.

street_sign.speaker: Visitor
street_sign.text: The name on the back has been erased. Several times.

window.speaker: Visitor
window.text: Warm windows. A kettle silhouette. Someone has drawn a curtain around an impossible amount of room.

window.speaker: Visitor
window.text: For a house that wasn't here yesterday, it looks very lived in.
